parsed.summary: The Lean statements prove that the Cohn–Elkies linear-programming bound LP_d = (v_d/2^d)·inf_{f∈A_d} f(0)/f̂(0) satisfies LP_d^{1/d} → √(e/(2π)), together with its base-2 log-rate form. They also prove the derived sphere-packing bound Δ_d ≤ (√(e/(2π)) + o(1))^d. A bundle of equivalent and auxiliary reformulations is included: root-of-infimum ~ √d/π, a uniform lower bound for all admissible f, and a 30-digit numeric certificate for α*. The definitions of A_d, LP_d, v_d and packing density match the paper's (1)–(4), and the Mathlib Fourier convention matches (1). The main caveat is coverage: Theorem 1.2 (the sign-uncertainty constants A±(d)/√d → 1/π) is not formalized.

glossary.standard_concept: volume of the unit ball in R^d
glossary.note: Γ(d/2+1) > 0 for d ≥ 0, so no pole and no junk division.

glossary.plain: A ℂ-valued Schwartz f on R^d that is real-valued, has real f̂ with f̂ ≥ 0 and f̂(0) > 0, and has f ≤ 0 on |x| ≥ 1.
glossary.note: Requiring f̂ to be real is implicit in the paper's condition f̂ ≥ 0. The Mathlib 𝓕 convention e^{-2πi⟨x,ξ⟩} matches (1).
The denominator is positive by fourier_zero_pos, so there is no junk division.
sInf is real-valued. The set is nonempty (A_d ≠ ∅) and bounded below by 0, since f(0) > 0 by Fourier inversion. Hence there is no junk value, at least asymptotically.

glossary.plain: A set of centers in R^d with pairwise distance ≥ separation > 0.
glossary.standard_concept: sphere packing with balls of radius separation/2

glossary.plain: limsup_{R→∞} vol(∪ balls ∩ B(0,R)) / vol B(0,R)
glossary.note: For R ≤ 0 the ratio is 0/0 = 0 in ℝ≥0∞, which does not affect the limsup at atTop.

glossary.plain: Δ_d = sup over packings of the upper density

lean_claims.plain: There is e(d) = o(1) such that for all d ≥ 1, Δ_d ≤ max(0, (√(e/(2π)) + e(d))^d).

All of the following hold: (i) inf_f (f(0)/f̂(0))^{1/d} / √d → 1/π, and this equals (1/π + err(d))√d for all d > 0 with err → 0; (ii) LP_d^{1/d} → √(e/2π); (iii) log LP_d / d → (1/2) log(e/2π); (iv) eventually LP_d = (√(e/2π) + err(d))^d; (v) there is δ ≥ 0 with δ → 0 such that eventually f(0)/f̂(0) ≥ (2^d/v_d)(√(e/2π) − δ(d))^d for every f ∈ A_d; (vi) α* = (1/2) log₂(2π/e) > 0 and lies in (0.604400544291677695341677307053, …054); (vii) log₂ LP_d / d → −α*; (viii) eventually LP_d = 2^{−(α* + err(d)) d} with err → 0.

coverage.why: Same limit, with the same definitions of LP_d, A_d and v_d.
(√(e/2π) + o(1))^d is the same as 2^{−(α* + o(1))d}. Also covered for LP_d by exact_binary_exponent.
No definition of r(g) or A_ς(d) appears. root_before_infimum is a packing-quotient analogue, not A±(d).

flags.explanation: The sign-uncertainty Theorem 1.2 (A₊, A₋ asymptotics) is not formalized anywhere. The root_before_infimum field concerns inf (f(0)/f̂(0))^{1/d} over A_d, not the Fourier-eigenfunction constants A_ς(d).
The 30-digit interval for α* is more precise than anything in the excerpt (which gives only 0.6044…). My hand computation agrees to about 10 digits. This is a stronger extra claim and harmless.
flags.probe_idea: norm_num/interval check of (1/2)·logb 2 (2π/e) against the stated bounds

flags.explanation: sInf over ℝ would be 0 if the quotient set were empty or unbounded below. Neither happens: the set is bounded below by 0 because f(0) > 0, and it is nonempty because A_d contains a Cohn–Elkies function. A degenerate LP_d = 0 would in any case contradict the stated limit.
flags.probe_idea: ∀ d ≥ 1, (fullQuotientSet d).Nonempty ∧ BddBelow (fullQuotientSet d) ∧ 0 < fullLinearProgram d
